avalanche_observations.area: North Tenmile Creek, south of West Deming

avalanche_detail.description: A very large avalanche was most likely remotely triggered from a long distance away on the opposite side of the ridge line. The party reported a very large collapse but couldn't see the other side of the ridge from where they were then observed this avalanche shortly after.

route: Hayden Mtn Backcountry lodge standard approach
description: Multiple wet loose avalanches on all aspects with direct sun, WL-N-R1-D1. Multiple E aspect crowns on a ridge S of Chicago Pk near ridge line. All displayed hard slab crowns, R1-R2, D1-D2. Suspect wind deposits overloading PWL. N aspect below ridge line crowns N of T8, they appeared older, estimate R1-D1. Light blowing snow. Generally light winds, warm daytime temps. Some melting surface hoar near valley bottoms.

avalanche_detail.description: A handful of small loose avalanches on south alpine slopes caused by sun warming a small amount of recent snowfall.

weather_detail.description: Warming quickly, but temperatures stayed right around freezing level at 12,000 ft. Calm winds increased around 11-12 o'clock coming from the southwest.

snowpack_detail.description:
On a northwest near treeline slope we failed to get propagating results (ECTX) despite a well-defined, strong (1 Finger) -over-weak (fist hard) structure.
Digging on a west slope above treeline we found evidence that moisture has passed through the snowpack to weak grains at the ground during last week's warm temperatures and superficial freezes. The snowpack structure on this aspect is shallower and stronger than on aspects that tilt more north.

assets.caption: West slopes are shallow due to warm weather and west/southwest prevailing winds. As you wrap around to northwest slopes there is more coverage and a defined strong-over-weak snowpack structure. Ohio Peak west and northwest-facing slopes.
assets.alternate_text: A peak with twigs and rocks poking through the snow.

assets.caption: Small superficial loose activity caused by warming of Friday's snow can be found on south alpine slopes.
assets.alternate_text: Small roller ball loose activity out of rocks on an alpine peak.

assets.caption: Near treeline around 11,900 feet on a northwest slope, we found recent snow above a 1-Finger slab over fist hard facets. Pit results: CT11 and ECTX.
assets.alternate_text: A ruler in a snowpit showing hand hardness

assets.caption: West around 12300 ft the snowpack is shallow, and facets have firmed beneath a 1 Finger slab. Steep rocky west slopes that hold snow may still have weaker facets beneath a slab in the alpine.
assets.alternate_text: A snow saw in a shallow pit with hand hardness showing 1 Finger and 4 Finger hardness.

objective: Gather info to hone in distribution of PSa on west aspects.
description: Happy to report that Friday's snow is still cold in the alpine on north tilting slopes. A few inches of recent snow sits on a supportable crust on these aspects. On south-facing slopes, recent snow has mostly melted and crusted in the alpine. Minor loose activity observed on some alpine souths from sun exposure over the last two days.
